description: A granular processor: it records what you patch into it and rebuilds it out of short overlapping grains whose pitch, length and read position you set

params.text: Sets how much of the buffer each grain reads, from none of it to all of it
Sets the chance that a voice starts a grain each time its cycle comes round, none of the time to every time
Sets the speed grains play back at, a third of normal speed to three times it
Widens the pitch each grain is given at random, none at the far left and three octaves either way at the far right; the offset is fixed when the grain starts and held for its life
Snaps grain speeds to step multiples of a ratio, free at the far left and locking hard to simple ratios at the far right
Tilts the fade shape of a grain, a fast attack at one end of its travel and a slow one at the other
Sets where in the buffer grains are read from, the oldest audio at one end of its travel and the newest at the other
Scatters each grain's read position away from the position knob, none at the far left and the whole buffer at the far right
Sets how widely grains are scattered left and right, mono at the far left and full width at the far right
Sets how much reverb is mixed into the granular signal, none at the far left
Sets the level of the incoming audio before it reaches the buffer, -18dB at the far left and +6dB at the far right
Sets the balance between the untouched input and the granular signal
Plays grains backwards while it is on, and flips the direction of grains already sounding on the next sample
Stops new audio being written into the buffer while it is on, so the grains go on reading what is already there

inputs.text: The left channel of the audio written into the buffer
Shifts the playback speed at 1V per octave, on top of the pitch knob
The right channel of the audio written into the buffer

outputs.text: The left channel of the granular signal mixed with the dry input
The right channel of the granular signal mixed with the dry input

notes: the buffer holds six seconds of audio and as many as 128 grains sound at once; how many is set from the menu
nothing comes out until audio is patched in, since the grains read a buffer that starts empty
with the pitch well up and the grain size large, the read position can land as much as eight per cent away from the knob to keep the buffer seam from clicking
menu: Soft clip — rounds the peaks of the output in place of letting it clip hard, and comes up off
Pitch knob: Repitch, Per-grain — Repitch moves grains already sounding as the knob turns; Per-grain leaves those at the speed they started with and gives the new speed to later grains
Grain Voices — sets how many grains can sound at once, from 4 up to 128
SSD1306 preview — a submenu for the small screen preview used when the patch is carried over to a Daisy board
Enable SSD1306 128x32 preview — inside SSD1306 preview; draws that preview on the panel or takes it away
Tint — inside SSD1306 preview; sets the colour the preview is drawn in

inputs.3:
1V per octave · continuous

unpatched it reads 0V.
